Long
LAWNG
adj.
Webster 1828 treats LONG as adjective from Latin longus: extended in a line; drawn out in time; tedious; continued in sound; the long home as the grave (Ecclesiastes 12:5). As adverb: to a great extent in space or time (Proverbs 23; Exodus 19:13); through the whole duration (Genesis 48:15). As verb intransitive: to desire earnestly (Romans 1:11; Psalm 119). This page fills the KJV-gap word of drawn-out time and holy craving. Companion pages already treat life, desire, and salvation.

Biblical Definition

Long in Scripture is not a playlist length and not a brand of patience. It names the drawn-out hour of refusal, the cry of the forgotten, the years of life God gives, and the ache of holy desire. Pharaoh is not negotiating: How long wilt thou refuse to humble thyself before me? (Exo 10:3). David is not journaling a mood: How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? (Psa 13:1). The promise is not a wellness span: With long life will I satisfy him, and shew him my salvation (Psa 91:16). The apostle will not hide the ache: For I long to see you (Rom 1:11). The commandment still carries a land: thou mayest live long on the earth (Eph 6:3). The dictionary therefore keeps long from becoming either delay or a craving app. It is the Bible’s way of saying: this far — and still, how long, O Lord.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines LONG as adjective from Latin longus: extended in line or time; tedious; the long home (Ecclesiastes 12:5). Adverb: to a great extent in space or time. Verb intransitive: to desire earnestly (Romans 1:11; Psalm 119).

expand to see more

LONG, adjective [Latin longus.]

1. Extended; drawn out in a line, or in the direction of length; opposed to short.

2. Drawn out or extended in time; as a long time; a long period of time; a long while.

3. Extended to any certain measure expressed; as a span long; a yard long.

4. Dilatory; continuing for an extended time.

5. Tedious; continued to a great length.

LONG home, the grave or death. Ecclesiastes 12:5.

LONG, adverb To a great extent in space; to a great extent in time. They that tarry long at the wine. Proverbs 23. When the trumpet soundeth long. Exodus 19:13.

The God who fed me all my life long to this day. Genesis 48:15.

LONG, verb intransitive

1. To desire earnestly or eagerly. I long to see you. Romans 1:11. I have longed after thy precepts. Psalms 119.

Key Scripture

Exo 10:3 — "And Moses and Aaron came in unto Pharaoh, and said unto him, Thus saith the LORD God of the Hebrews, How long wilt thou refuse to humble thyself before me? let my people go, that they may serve me."

Psa 13:1 — "To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David. How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?"

Psa 91:16 — "With long life will I satisfy him, and shew him my salvation."

Rom 1:11 — "For I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, to the end ye may be established;"

Eph 6:3 — "That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth."

Modern Corruption

Long is corrupted when duration is emptied of the Lord’s question, when how-long is recast as a complaint brand, and when long life is sold as self-care span without salvation.

expand to see more

The first corruption is Exodus 10:3 as a negotiation. How long wilt thou refuse to humble thyself is the Lord’s question to Pharaoh. Delay is not diplomacy. The recovery is humble now.

The second corruption is Psalm 13:1 as content. How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? is petition, not a thread. The hidden face is real. The cry is to Him.

The third corruption is Psalm 91:16 as a longevity plan. With long life will I satisfy him, and shew him my salvation is gift and salvation together. Romans 1:11 longs to impart a gift, not a vibe. Ephesians 6:3 lives long on the earth under commandment — not under a biohack.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Webster: Latin longus. Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Hebrew orek (H753) at Psalm 91:16 on long; Greek epipotheo (G1971) at Romans 1:11; makrochronios (G3118) at Ephesians 6:3. Exodus 10:3 carries no Strong’s tag on long in this cache; Psalm 13:1 tags the following verbs (forget H7911 / hide H5641). This page does not mint a leftover lemma.

expand to see more

Hebrew orek (H753) — length (Psa 91:16, long life).

Greek epipotheo (G1971) — to long for (Rom 1:11, I long to see you); makrochronios (G3118) at Ephesians 6:3 (live long on the earth).

Exodus 10:3 is KJV-verified; the cache does not tag English long with a Hebrew number on that verse line. Psalm 13:1 tags forget (H7911) and hide (H5641) after how long. No lemma is invented for the particle.

Usage

"Pharaoh: how long wilt thou refuse to humble thyself (Exo 10:3)."

"David: how long wilt Thou forget me (Psa 13:1); long life with salvation (Psa 91:16)."

"Paul: I long to see you (Rom 1:11); live long on the earth (Eph 6:3)."
